newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end weaker, underperform U.S. issues.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end weaker, underperform U.S. issues.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker on Tuesday, with spreads to U.S. long bonds widening amid stronger than expected U.S. consumer confidence data and a sliding Canadian dollar, analysts said.

"It's the first time we've closed through seven percent in the U.S. since the end of April. That was driven to some extent by that very strong consumer confidence number this morning. That has led the markets lower," said Jim Webber, director of fixed-income research with TD Securities Inc.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$1.00 to C$110.15 to yield 7.136 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 15/32 to yield 7.03 percent. The spread between the bonds widened to 11 basis points from seven basis points at the close of trading on Monday.

Canadian bonds weakened this morning with U.S. treasuries on a report that an index of U.S. consumer confidence surged in May to a 28-year high. The data sparked concern the U.S. Federal Reserve was now more likely to hike rates at the next meeting of its Open Market Committee.
Also hurting Canadian bonds was a slide in the currency, which was hit by pre-election jitters. The weakness prompted two rounds of intervention by the Bank of Canada.
"Everybody was very clear a week ago on how they thought it (election) was going to go. There's just a bit more uncertainty now about how that's going to end up," said TD's Webber.
In the short end, dealers said there was uneven demand for this afternoon's auction of C$4.4 billion three-month, six-month and one-year T-bills.
"Technically, the market wasn't set up well for the market today," said one T-bill trader with a bank-owned brokerage. "The one-years were quite sloppy."
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.57 to C$102.78 to yield 6.597 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 9/32 to yield 6.79 percent.
The negative spread between the two bonds narrowed to 19 basis points from 23 basis points at the close of trading on Monday.
The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 3.03 percent against its U.S. equivalent, which yielded 5.18 percent.
